headline: Hawaii Erases $91 Million in Medical Debt for 50,000 Residents
meta_description: Hawaii signed healthcare measures to cancel up to $91 million in medical debt for 50,000 qualified residents through simple letter notification.
summary_short: Hawaii just signed healthcare measures that could erase up to $91 million in medical debt for 50,000 residents, with qualified people simply receiving a letter.
body:
Hawaii has signed healthcare measures that could cancel up to $91 million in medical debt affecting 50,000 residents across the islands.

The program's simplicity stands out: qualified individuals will receive a letter notifying them their debt has been erased. There is no application process, no forms to fill out—just notification of relief. This straightforward approach removes barriers that often prevent people from accessing debt forgiveness programs they qualify for.

The move reflects a growing recognition that medical debt can trap families in cycles of financial hardship, even when they have insurance. By automatically canceling debt for qualifying residents, Hawaii removes that burden without requiring people to navigate complex bureaucracy.
quick_facts: Hawaii enacted healthcare measures canceling medical debt
Up to $91 million in debt affected
Qualified people notified via letter only
